title: RBACv2 switchboard: sampling backfill, dual-write safeguards, validation gates, and customer comms schedule
creator: Priya Patel
description: Goal: perform a low-risk production migration from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 by running a controlled dual-write, performing sampled backfills, validating consistency with automated gates, and executing a staged cutover with customer communications. This ticket defines the sampling strategy, validation automation, rollback criteria, SSO/role-mapping checks, audit-log continuity plan, and the customer notification schedule. Key constraints: zero downtime for authentication paths, preservation of audit trails, and minimal spike in token-service latency (<15% tail).
acceptance_criteria: Dual-write enabled for 10% of requests for 48h with end-to-end success rate >= 99.9%
Backfill sampler runs and completes consistency checks for 1000 random orgs with <0.1% mismatches after reconciliation
SAML role mappings validated against canonical mapping table and SSO test orgs pass login + mapping assertions
Audit log forwarding preserves original actor, timestamp, and change diff for v1 and v2 entries for 30 days
Automated rollback triggers on: mismatch rate >0.5% for critical roles OR error rate increase >3x baseline OR latency P99 regression >20%
Runbook reviewed and approved by Security and Support with signoff documented
Customer comms doc published and scheduled with support FAQ and opt-out guidance
steps: 1) Build dual-write shim in auth-service: write to v1 authoritative store and v2 canonical store with idempotent keys
2) Deploy dual-write behind flag; enable for internal orgs + canary customers
3) Implement sampled backfill pipeline that pulls delta between v1 and v2 and writes reconciliation patches into a staging queue
4) Run automated validators: role-count parity, permission bitmask diff, and SAML assertion replay tests
5) Measure audit log parity via nightly batch job comparing event hashes and schema fields
6) Expand sampling window progressively (1%, 5%, 10%) and validate gates between phases
7) Initiate broad backfill for remaining tenants with throttling and monitoring windows
8) Coordinate final cutover window with Support/PM/Legal and publish customer migration notice 7 days prior
9) Flip authoritative flag after successful 72h stable window; keep v1 read-only for 30 days before deprecation
10) Post-cutover: execute retention audit for logs, run reconciliation sweep, and publish migration report

notes: Trade-offs discussed: stricter pre-cutover validation versus speed of migration. Agreed to conservative gates to protect enterprise customers.
Rollback plan favors quick disable of dual-write and redirecting reads to v1 authoritative store; v2 writes marked but not used for auth until next attempt.
Backfill throttling default: 500 orgs/hour with exponential backoff on transient DB errors to avoid primary-db overload.
We will maintain v1 read-only access for 30 days post-cutover to allow support-driven reconciliation and forensics.
Edge case: orgs with custom role templates must be whitelisted for manual verification prior to broad backfill; PM to own list.
